summary: Interpreted the retained receipt for the liveness-witness revision (CheckRun 35a6c1074291424686f0360747f6c268: completed, tests_passed, exit 0, 17 parsed observations, 0 parse errors). Indices 0-15 reproduce probes A-C; index 16 is the sweep summary with seeds=60, steps_per_seed=60, elections=466, ordinary proposals=452, conf_change_proposals=249, restarts=471, stalled_states=0, violations=0. Recorded as holds-only with the defect claim refuted narrowly: the witness fires only when a node holds a committed-but-unapplied configuration change and no node is promotable, exactly the state where the campaign admission guard could cost a cluster its leader, and it never fired - so within this event set the guard's suppression never coincided with a configuration that had no candidate able to campaign. I also answered gap 984747de5ed94b4ea8f6977b2a92808f-gap-2 on the evidence now available, deliberately leaving it unresolved: the event-set items it named (simple and joint configuration changes, a real joining participant, restarts that adopt the ConfState storage supplies) are covered by the three earlier receipts plus this one, but demotion of an existing serving voter, storage faults and per-occurrence witness operands were not exercised, and a zero count is not a bound. Counterevidence kept explicit: the witness is only evaluated at the check point after each event, so a brief leaderless configuration between checks would be missed; zero occurrences cannot distinguish 'the guard never had this cost' from 'the event mix rarely produces the antecedent', since the sweep does not record how often any node had an unapplied change at all; and the counter totals occurrences without operands, so it supports the negative only as scoped and could not diagnose an occurrence. Remaining work if the run continues: per-occurrence witness operands, demotion of an existing voter, and storage/applied-lag variations that the harness still models optimistically.
